fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the street entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so the travel path remains clear to a height of at least 14 feet for fire apparatus and other emergency vehicles.
• Clear vegetation on both sides of the driveway to a width that allows a full-size emergency vehicle to pass without obstruction.
• Create a turnaround area near the residence or detached structure large enough for emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around the buildings on foot.
• Trim vegetation near the detached structure so responders can quickly identify and reach all sides of the building.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without pushing through overgrowth.
• Mark any gate or entry point along the driveway with reflective indicators and keep it unlocked or secured with a standard knox-type lock box.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored equipment or materials that would block emergency vehicles from reaching the residence.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls and foundation.
• Thin trees around the house to create open gaps between tree canopies and the structure.
• Remove tall grass from the area immediately surrounding the house and any outbuildings.
• Cut or mow the tall grass area down before dry season to reduce the amount of burnable material close to the structure.
• Separate shrubs from nearby trees by removing shrubs growing directly beneath tree canopies.
• Clear dead grass, dry leaves, and loose plant debris from the ground around the house regularly.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure by removing selected trees to break up the dense grouping.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches that could block emergency vehicle access.
• Mow or cut grass growing along both sides of the driveway to keep a clear travel path.
• Remove any shrubs or low branches along the driveway that narrow the vehicle travel lane.
• Keep the area around any gates or entry points to the driveway clear so vehicles can pass without stopping.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders approaching from the main road.
• Thin scattered trees on the uphill or windward sides of the house more aggressively than other sides.
